blocks.text: Tuple bhi list ki tarah cheezon ka ordered collection (tarteeb wala majmua) hai, magar ek bara farq hai: tuple immutable (na badalne wala) hai, yani banne ke baad us ki values badli nahi ja saktin. Tuple brackets ( ) mein likha jata hai.

# Creating a tuple
my_tuple = (1, 2, 3, "Hello", 4.5)

# Accessing elements by index
print(my_tuple[0])  # Output: 1
print(my_tuple[3])  # Output: Hello

# Tuple length
print(len(my_tuple))  # Output: 5

blocks.title: Code Explanation (Wazahat)
blocks.text:
"# Creating a tuple" jaisi # wali lines comments hain; yeh chalti nahi.
"my_tuple = (1, 2, 3, "Hello", 4.5)": round brackets ( ) mein paanch items ka tuple banta hai; is mein numbers, string aur decimal sab mile jule hain.
"print(my_tuple[0])": index 0 wala pehla item: 1.
"print(my_tuple[3])": index 3 wala chautha item: Hello (print string ko quotes ke baghair dikhata hai).
"print(len(my_tuple))": len() items ginta hai: 5.
Output: teen lines: 1, Hello aur 5.
Khud try karein: aakhir mein my_tuple[0] = 10 likh kar Run karein: TypeError aayega ('tuple' object does not support item assignment), kyunke tuple immutable (na badalne wala) hai.

blocks.prompt: my_tuple[0] = 10 karne ki koshish par kya hota hai?
blocks.explanation: Python TypeError deti hai, kyunke tuple badla nahi ja sakta.

items: Tuple: ( ) mein; index se parhte hain; badal nahi sakte (immutable).
